'''Rudolf Paul Joachim Kochendörffer''' (21 November 1911 in [[Pankow]] &ndash; 23 August 1980 in [[Dortmund]]) was a [[German people|German]] [[mathematician]] and professor of mathematics in the [[University of Rostock]] specialising in [[algebra]], [[group theory]] and theory of [[finite group]]s and their representation.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=20713}}</ref><ref name="ros">{{cite web|title=Kochendörffer, Rudolf|url=http://cpr.uni-rostock.de/resolve/id/cpr_person_00001330|website=University of Rostock|publisher=Catalogus Professorum Rostochiensium|accessdate=23 October 2017}}</ref> During [[World War II]], Kochendörffer worked as a  mathematical [[cryptanalysis|cryptanalyst]] in the mathematical referat of Inspectorate 7/IV, that would later become part of Referat I of Group IV of the [[General der Nachrichtenaufklärung]] (abbr. GDNA), the [[signals intelligence]] agency of the [[Wehrmacht]] and was known as a cryptographic tester of the [[Enigma machine|Enigma]] cipher machine.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Kochendörffer|first1=Rudolf|title=DF-38 The Enigma|url=https://archive.org/details/ticom/Df-38TheEnigma|website=Internet Archive|publisher=TICOM|accessdate=11 June 2026}}</ref> Kochendörffer was a Member of the Scientific Advisory Council for Mathematics at the State Secretariat for the Higher and Specialist Schools of the GDR, a staff member of [[Mathematical Reviews]] and collaborated with the [[Zentralblatt MATH]]<ref name="ros"/>

==Life==
Rudolf Kochendörffer's father, Albert Kochendörffer(1877-1958) was a lending bookseller ({{langx|de|Leihbuchhändler}}). His mother was Bertha Kochendörffer. 
==Education==
In 1930, Kochendörffer completed his [[Abitur]]. Kochendörffer subsequently studied at the [[Technische Hochschule]] in Charlottenburg (now [[Technische Universität Berlin]]) from 1930 to 1936 on the study of [[mathematics]], [[physics]] and [[philosophy]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Kalliope-Verbund|url=http://kalliope.staatsbibliothek-berlin.de/de/eac?eac.id=116273615|website=Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin - Prussian Cultural HeritaStaatsbibliothek zu Berlinge|publisher=Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation|accessdate=24 October 2017}}</ref>

==Career==
In 1936, he was promoted to [[Doctor of Philosophy|Dr Phil]], with a doctoral thesis titled: ''Investigations on a presumption of [[William Burnside|W. Burnside]]'' (German:Untersuchungen über eine Vermutung von W. Burnside) ([[Burnside's theorem]]). His doctoral advisors where [[Ludwig Bieberbach]], [[Issai Schur]] and [[Erhard Schmidt]]. He was forced to resign as a Jew in 1935. During 1938-1939 he worked as an assistant at the [[University of Göttingen]].

During the war Kochendörffer worked as a cryptanalyst, from 1939 to 1942 as an assistant in the cryptanalysis department [[Pers Z S]] of the [[Federal Foreign Office|Foreign Office]] and from 1942-1945 in the [[Cipher Department of the High Command of the Wehrmacht|OKW/Chi]] and the GDNA. He documented the breaking of the Swiss [[Enigma machine#Enigma K|Enigma K]] machine and was part of the team, with [[Hans-Peter Luzius]] and [[Willi Rinow]], that broke the [[M-209]] code.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Frode Weierud |author2=Sandy Zabell |title=German mathematicians and cryptology in WWII |journal=Cryptologia |volume=44 |issue=2 |year=2020 |pages=97-171 |doi=10.1080/01611194.2019.1600076}}</ref>

From 1946 to 1948 Kochendörffer worked as a Senior assistant at the Mathematical Institute of the [[Humboldt University of Berlin]]. In 1948, Kochendörffer  [[Habilitation|habilitated]] in the subjects of mathematics in Berlin, and was promoted to full [[professor]]. He then appointed to position as professor of mathematics at the [[University of Greifswald]], for a year. 

In 1950, Kochendörffer became a professor of Mathematics at the [[University of Rostock]], a position he held until 1966.<ref name="ros"/>Kochendörffer specialized in [[group theory]]. He was also published algebra textbooks. Between 1967-1970 Kochendörffer was visiting professor of Mathematics, Faculty of Natural Sciences at the [[Johannes Gutenberg University of Mainz]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Prof. Dr. Rudolf Kochendörffer|url=http://gutenberg-biographics.ub.uni-mainz.de/id/e3c352dc-8175-4cd6-a21c-63e1c918cbce|website=Johannes Gutenberg-Universität Mainz, Universitätsbibliothek|publisher=Gutenberg Biographics|accessdate=24 October 2017}}</ref> and at the [[University of Tasmania]]. Between 1970-1977, Kochendörffer finished his career as professor of Mathematics at [[TU Dortmund University]].<ref name="ros"/>

He was a member of the {{ill|Mathematische Gesellschaft der DDR|de}}, [[German Mathematical Society]] and the member of [[Gesellschaft für Angewandte Mathematik und Mechanik]].<ref name="ros"/>

==Awards and honours==
In 1960, he was awarded the [[Patriotic Order of Merit]] in Bronze, which was recognized in 1967. In 1963 he received the [[National Prize of the German Democratic Republic]], National Prize III. for science and technology.

==Publications==
* Einführung in die Algebra. Berlin 1955, 4. Aufl. 1974. (English Edition: Introduction to algebra. Groningen 1972).
* Determinants and matrices (German:Determinanten und Matrizen). Leipzig 1957, 5. Aufl. 1967. (License Issue Stuttgart 1970).
* Lehrbuch der Gruppentheorie. Unter besonderer Berücksichtigung der endlichen Gruppen. Leipzig 1966. (English Edition: Textbook of the group theory with special consideration of the finite groups. Leipzig 1966, English Group Theory, McGraw Hill 1970).
* On supplements of finite groups. Groningen 1963.
